faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are industry-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Commission, often higher than the minimum wage. Your pay must meet the higher of the two.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual with Tax and Super

Our **take home pay after salary sacrifice calculator** helps you estimate your net income based on your hourly rate, assuming a standard 38-hour week and no salary packaging. While it doesn't account for salary sacrifice arrangements, it gives you a clear baseline to compare job offers or understand your current pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

To convert an hourly rate to annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So the formula is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on our site lets you enter your exact hours and includes an option to add casual loading.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $30/hour example, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. This is before tax and super. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing to pay cycles.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.

However, most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award have specific rates for different classifications. Always check your award to ensure you're being paid correctly. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on current rates.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum rate from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When using our calculator, if you are casual, you can tick the "Add 25% casual loading" checkbox. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading; the calculator adds it for you. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for more.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to your employer. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter (2026-27). For most workers, super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, including overtime if it's regular.

For example, on a $59,280 annual salary, the employer would contribute $7,113.60 in super (12% of $59,280). This goes into your super fund and is taxed at 15% within the fund. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more about how super interacts with salary packaging.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay depends on tax brackets and the Medicare levy. For 2026-27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax-free threshold of $18,200 means you pay no tax on the first $18,200. Using the $59,280 example, tax would be approximately $9,267 (calculated on the brackets) plus Medicare of $1,185.60, leaving about $48,827 after tax and Medicare. This is an estimate; your actual tax may vary due to offsets, deductions, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

Note: The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles used here are from 2025-26, as the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. The Australian Taxation Office provides the latest rates.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data, which shows differences across states and territories. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week nationally. However, this average masks variation: earnings in New South Wales and Victoria tend to be higher than in Tasmania or South Australia, reflecting industry mix and cost of living. The ABS also reports all employees total earnings (including part-time) at $1,579.20 per week.

When comparing job offers across states, consider that the same hourly rate may result in different take-home pay due to state taxes? No, state taxes are not income taxes; only federal. But cost of living and award rates may differ. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more on state-by-state data.

### Important Disclaimer

This calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes a consistent hourly rate, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a precise determination, consult a tax professional or use the ATO's tax estimator.

Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page offers more resources, and the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains the formula in detail. While this take home pay after salary sacrifice calculator does not adjust for salary packaging, it provides a useful starting point for understanding your earnings.
